gaps.what: Modifications to DCPR 2034 after 8 May 2018, among them the 14 Oct 2024 notification on premium and TDR and the Reg 30(A) road-widening order
gaps.why: The only machine-readable official text is the 2018 sanctioned text. The 2024 notification PDF has a garbled legacy-font text layer, and Table 12 Note 2 lets the Government change the premium and TDR split. This pack is a draft as sanctioned in 2018.

gaps.what: Tower open spaces and step-backs above 32 m, 70 m and 120 m (Reg 41(2)(c), p289), the dead-wall column of Table A and its 4.5 m minimum for commercial buildings
gaps.why: Plotwise applies the light-and-ventilation column of Table A for a residential building on every side but the front, at the height of each floor, as a step-back would; it assumes every side has windows, so the smaller dead-wall open space is never used. The tower rules are not applied.

gaps.what: The road-height rule ceasing for plots with a 9 m or 12 m front margin, and aerodrome height limits (Reg 43(1), Reg 43(B))
gaps.why: Not modelled; the road-height rule is applied to every plot.

gaps.what: Whether the Table 12 road width is the existing or the prescribed width
gaps.why: Table 12 Note 1 moves a 6 m to 9 m road proposed to be widened to the 9 m row. Plotwise reads every band, and the height rule, from the widened width once a prescribed width is entered.

gaps.what: Annual Schedule of Rates land value for the plot
gaps.why: Published only through the eASR web form at easr.igrmaharashtra.gov.in, one zone at a time. It is entered by the user.
No official price; Reg 32 fixes how much TDR is generated, not its price. It is entered by the user.

gaps.what: Which plots are in the R zone of the suburbs, and the DP road widths and regular lines
gaps.why: They are on the development plan maps, not in the DCPR text. The user confirms the zone and enters any prescribed road width.
This draft covers residential buildings in the R zone only.
Reg 41(1) to (3) set no general coverage share for this zone; coverage follows from the open spaces and FSI.

gaps.what: Inclusive housing on plots of 4000 m² or more (Reg 15), layout open space and amenity handover (Reg 27, Reg 14), and FSI-exempt areas (Reg 31(1))
Development cess and the development charge
gaps.why: Reg 30(A)(7) sets a cess of 100% of the development charge, whose rate was not read.

gaps.what: The column of each repeated Table 12 value (0.5 premium and 0.5 TDR on the 9 m row, 1.0 basic and 1.0 TDR on the 27 m row)
gaps.why: The text layer cannot say which column a repeated value sits in; the values are equal, so the numbers are right but the cite is to the line.

gaps.what: Whether Table No 17 replaces Table A and Table 18 A or only relaxes them
gaps.why: Reg 41(3)(a) says the open spaces may be relaxed to Table No 17; Plotwise applies it to the checks of a building of ground and one upper floor on a plot it covers, and keeps the envelope on the stricter open spaces. The rear is taken as the boundary edge farthest from the main road.

gaps.what: How Table A measures the average width and depth of a plot, and a plot of more than 1000 m² whose average width or depth is exactly 20 m
gaps.why: DCPR 2034 does not define them. Plotwise measures the plot left after any road-widening strip, along and across its main road (area over its depth, area over its width), and puts a plot that is not up to 1000 m² and not under 20 m wide or deep in the larger plot class, whose open spaces are larger. Table A leaves buildings above 70 m on the smaller plot class blank, so Plotwise draws none.
